observation_review.reasoning: Prediction assumed hand-folding edges under 'slightly' creates a flat stable foot. Report is explicitly hypothetical-test, not a physical trial, so no verified measurement exists. Even as an imagined model, perfect flatness is questionable: folding cardboard creates localized double-thickness at corners, and the taped ring adds a central raised feature. Analysis notes typical construction would expect such thickness variation to prevent true flatness. Mismatch therefore reflects an idealized assumption, not proven model failure.

possible_explanations.explanation: Folded-under edges create uneven thickness, especially where corners overlap, forming a high point so the base contacts on one corner first and rocks.
possible_explanations.distinguishing_observation: Place existing base lightly on a flat table and at eye level look for light under edges, or try sliding a thin paper strip under each corner to see uneven contact, without pressing or modifying.

possible_explanations.explanation: Taped folded ring in center adds localized tape and cardboard thickness that can bow or stiffen the thin base, lifting the center and leaving corners as pivot points in an idealized probe.
possible_explanations.distinguishing_observation: Visually inspect underside for tape buildup or bowing under the ring area and compare center height to corners while model rests untouched.

possible_explanations.explanation: Because report_type is hypothetical-test, the rocking result is an imagined idealization ignoring cardboard compliance, friction and real table variation, not evidence of actual physical behavior.
possible_explanations.distinguishing_observation: Note report states no physical trial; simply observe the real craft piece at rest on a table without tapping to see if it actually rocks, recognizing this remains a visual check only.

limits: Review interprets text report only, not independent verification of original fan or craft model
No dimensions, materials testing, or stability measurements were supplied in analysis or report
Real cardboard behavior varies with fold precision and humidity and cannot be inferred from hypothetical probe
Do not modify original fan or add power/tools to test stability

learning.title: Review: Flared Pedestal Base Stability — Craft Study
learning.answer: The supplied analysis identifies the foreground object as a vintage GE table fan with a flared pedestal base (part-4), wire guard cage (part-1), blades/hub (part-2) and motor housing (part-5) — all inferred from frontal form, not measured. The separate craft study aimed to illustrate the principle of stable mounting / tipping resistance (wide flared foot) without reproducing airflow or electrics. The prediction (flat, non-rocking) and the reported 'different' outcome (one corner touches first, rocks) are distinct: the report is explicitly a hypothetical software probe only, not a physical trial, so it provides no independent verification. The prediction's assumption of perfect flatness from folded cardboard is questionable and does not imply the heritage design is unstable.
safety_notes: No handling, powering, or disassembly of the antique fan — review uses only the text report
If inspecting the separate cardboard model, keep fingers clear of binder clips and small parts away from young children
limitations: This review does not test real airflow, motor function, material strength, or historical manufacturing
Paper/cardboard analogue cannot reproduce cast-metal stiffness, weight, or screw-mounted stability of the actual pedestal
Hypothetical probe provides no measured flatness, load, or vibration data
